newsitem.title: USA: Microprocessor market to grow 18 pct/yr- Dataquest.
newsitem.headline: Microprocessor market to grow 18 pct/yr- Dataquest.

text.p: The worldwide microprocessor market is poised to grow at an average of 18 percent per year through the year 2000, according to a new study by market research firm Dataquest.

The technology research firm said it expects the world microprocessor market to reach $17.1 billion in 1996, up from $14.2 billion in 1995. It sees microprocessors generating $33.6 million in revenues by the year 2000.
Microprocessors are the key integrated circuits that form the computational "brains" inside computers.

Dataquest said its analysts expect the CISC, or Complex Instructional Set Computing semgment of the microprocessor business, which Intel Corp dominates, to be the most profitable area in the entire semiconductor market.
"The good news is that a pot of gold awaits any vendor able to achieve success in this market," said Nathan Brookwood, principal analyst in Dataquest's Semiconductor Applications program.
"The bad news is that Intel stands watch over this pot of gold, and any contender must first defeat, or at least distract, Intel before reaping any benefits in this market," he said.
Dataquest also predicted the embedded microprocessor market will grow at a compound growth rate of 12 percent through the year 2000.

Embedded microprocessors are computer chips which are embedded in a larger machine such as consumer electronics, home appliances, automobiles and other manufacturered goods. The microprocessor that controls a car engine is an example.
The market is forecast to grow from $1.8 billion in 1995 to $3.1 billion as the 21st century starts, it said.
